mappings.note: Name AND structure of a four-carbon alcohol. Both demands are graded, so both LO-4s are cited; naming leads because it fixes the chain length and the -OH group. Same treatment as the three-carbon twin, sha 786bd77696af0540.
Name AND structure of a four-carbon aldehyde - same dual demand as the alcohol twin, differing only in functional group.
Names hydrogenation of vegetable oil - an addition reaction. No outcome covers reaction types; competency-level C 1.3 cited.
Sooty yellow flame from incomplete combustion of an unsaturated hydrocarbon. Combustion and flame have no outcome in this frame; C 1.3 competency cited.
Whether combustion always shows a flame. Same combustion gap; C 1.3 competency.
Combustion is exothermic - classifying a chemical change by energy, which sits under C 1.3 at competency level; no outcome covers it.
Identifies the ketone and carboxylic acid groups from condensed formulae - 'identifies functional groups', LO-4.
Derives butanol from butane, i.e. replaces a hydrogen with -OH to move between series. Functional group plus series reasoning, LO-4; only a molecular formula is wanted, so not C 1.3-LO-4.
Only a structural formula is asked for (propene), so C 1.3-LO-4 alone - contrast the 'name and structure' items, which carry C 1.1-LO-4 as well.
Vinegar as dilute ethanoic acid - a property/use of ethanoic acid, LO-8. Duplicate target of the MCQ sha cfc5bbc527cf0cf6.

Writes the electron dot structure of ethane, a carbon compound - LO-4 of C 1.3 exactly. Its bond-count twin (sha 655d34c09582a925) goes to C 1.1-LO-3 instead, because that one asks for a number, not a representation.
Number of covalent bonds in ethane. Bond counting applies tetravalency plus one catenation bond, so LO-3; the representation twin of this item is sha c1bcbf798f79934f.
Bond count for propane - same tetravalency-plus-catenation rule as ethane and butane. This trio honestly shares one outcome.
Names the -OH and >C=O groups - 'identifies functional groups', LO-4.
Bond count for butane - same family and same outcome as the ethane and propane counts.
Why atoms bond at all (octet/inert-gas stability). General bonding from atomic structure, which is C 1.1; nothing carbon-specific, so no outcome applies.
Bond in N2. Not a carbon compound, so C 1.3-LO-4 does not reach it; C 1.1 (compound formation from valency) cited.

Why covalent compounds conduct poorly (no free ions). The frame has no outcome for the physical properties of covalent compounds; competency cited, and this is the explanatory version of the MCQ family at sha 335c51066a89387f.
Draws the electron dot structure of CH3Cl, a carbon compound - LO-4 of C 1.3 applies directly.
Names the series with general formula CnH2n-2 (alkynes) - LO-4, the twin of the CnH2n item at sha aa4771cb114ad019.
Draws the structure of ethene - a representation task on a carbon compound, C 1.3-LO-4.
Alcohol is neutral to litmus - a chemical property of ethanol, LO-8. Contrasted with ethanoic acid's acidity elsewhere in the chapter, which is the same outcome.
Bond in O2. Non-carbon molecule, so outside C 1.3-LO-4's wording; C 1.1 cited, as for the N2 twin.
POOR FIT. Industrial production of alcohol by fermentation is a preparation, and LO-8 covers only properties; cited because it is the sole code naming ethanol. Same gap as sha b1a4e10b1c037975.
